title: Watermelon Ice Pops with a Lime Sherbet Rind
changes_from_base: Sieved watermelon frozen to a slush with chocolate-chip "seeds" replaces the strawberry purée, topped with a lime sherbet "rind" in paper tubs.
summary: Watermelon ice pops studded with tiny chocolate chips and finished with a pale sherbet rind to mimic the look of a watermelon slice.
equipment: twelve 90 ml paper or plastic tubs

ingredients.item: watermelon flesh (from ½ small seedless watermelon)

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend about 1.2 litres watermelon flesh with 100 g caster sugar in batches until smooth, then push through a sieve.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Cover and freeze for 2-3 h until slushy but not solid, then stir well, scraping the sides, and stir in 45 g mini chocolate chips.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Stand twelve 90 ml tubs in a tin and spoon in the slush to 1 cm below the rims, then freeze for 1-2 h until solid but not rock hard.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Spread the softened lime sherbet over the top as a rind layer, right to the rim.

steps.title: Seal
steps.text: Cover each tub with cling film, cut a small slit and push a stick in almost to the bottom.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 5 h, up to 2 days.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stand for 1 min, then pull the pops out or peel away the paper tubs.

tips: Stir the slush well before filling the tubs so the chocolate chips stay evenly spread rather than sinking.
Let the watermelon layer firm up before adding the sherbet rind, or the two layers will blend together.
Push the stick in carefully through the slit so it sits centred and upright.
storage: Keep the pops in their tubs or wrapped individually in the freezer.
